Asked for an open-source, self-hosted alternative to LaunchDarkly, a commenter recommended Unleash (github.com/Unleash/unleash). They described it as a feature toggle system that gives an overview of toggles across all applications and services, with official clients for Java, Node.js, Go, Ruby and Python.

Criticism of Unleash's published feature-flag principles: item 1 ("Enable run-time control") is "almost exclusively focused on what to do but not on why." It skips use-cases, assumptions, benefits and drawbacks. Another commenter added it reads like "describing how a product works, being passed off as knowledge."
Positive reaction to Unleash open-sourcing its feature-flag principles and inviting PRs on GitHub: "Open Source knowledge sharing. I like it."

Unleash user: "We use Unleash. There are many things you can do with feature flags and Unleash helps with a lot of them. However, my feeling is 80% of the value comes from 20% of the features. Even a much simpler system provides a ton of benefit."

A user who spent a day evaluating self-hosted flag tools (Java/Ruby SDKs, PostgreSQL, remote config, UI, local caching) found Unleash "impressive and powerful, but its UI is more complex than needed, and it lacks remote configuration." They leaned toward FeatureHub, but said if remote config isn't needed, Unleash offers more features than Flagsmith, Flipt or FeatureHub.

An engineer on Block/Square's internal flag team, with LaunchDarkly experience, compared targeting rules. LaunchDarkly offers ordered rules with ANDed conditions, while "many open source solutions (Unleash, last I checked, some time ago) are more limited: some of them don't let you vary on inputs, some only a small set of prescribed attributes."
A commenter praised Unleash publishing its feature flag principles as open source: "Open Source knowledge sharing. I like it."
A reader of Unleash's principles docs complained: "I couldn't find an easy link from these docs to the product page on mobile... I had to edit the URL to get to the company website."
